author: Trevor King
title: Michigan to take on Howard in March Madness opening round - NewsBreak
text:
By Trevor King ,
9 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Michigan men’s basketball has claimed a top spot in the NCAA men’s college basketball championship tournament and will take on Howard University on Thursday.
Michigan steamrolled its way through nearly every opponent it faced all year, finishing the season 31-3, the best record in the program’s history and the best in the Big Ten. Michigan’s dominance was more than enough to ensure the boys in blue a No. 1 seed in the tournament.
Howard earned its 16 seed tournament bid on Tuesday after defeating the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) Retrivers in an 86-83 thriller in a First Four matchup.
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – MARCH 15: Yaxel Lendeborg #23 of the Michigan Wolverines celebrates against the Purdue Boilermakers during the first half of the 2026 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Tournament Championship game at the United Center on March 15, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) According to Basketball Reference , this is the second time in history that the two teams will face off. In the first and only matchup, the Wolverines defeated the Bison 76-58.
The two teams will play in the round of 64 on March 19, with tip-off scheduled for 7:10 p.m. at the KeyBank Center in Buffalo, New York.
The winner of the game will face either the 8-seed Georgia or the 9-seed St. Louis on Saturday.
Information on how to watch the game is available at the bottom of this page. Michigan Michigan played arguably the best season in school history this year and is one of the favorites to claim the national championship.
As previously mentioned, the Wolverines dominated both Big Ten and out-of-conference play. They finished with an in-conference record of 19-1, with the only loss occurring at the Crisler Center against Wisconsin in January. Michigan lost only one other regular-season game all year, falling to national championship favorite Duke in January.
Purdue took down Michigan in the Big Ten tournament championship, 80-72.
While the team may have ended the regular season on a sour note, the Wolverines are built for March.
Michigan didn’t just beat teams this season; in many of those games they dismantled its opponents. They broke the Big Ten record for the most 40-point victories in a season, notching six. This dominance wasn’t isolated to these games. The Wolverines ranked 5th in scoring margin in the NCAA, beating opponents by an average of 17 points per game.
Michigan is the only team in all of college basketball to rank in the top 10 in offensive efficiency and defensive efficiency.
Senior forward Yaxel Lendeborg has been a force throughout the season, using his size and strong all-around game to impose his will on the court. He was named Big Ten player of the year and a First Team All-American. UAB transfer averaged 14.6 points, 7 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.3 blocks, and 1.2 steals a night on 50.9% from the field.
Lendeborg is projected to be a late lottery pick in the upcoming NBA draft in June.
Junior Aday Mara, the Spanish-born 7-foot-3 center, is one of the best defensive bigs in the nation. The Big Ten defensive player of the year averaged 2.6 blocks, third best in the country, and 6.9 rebounds while also putting up 11.6 points a night. Mara transferred to Michigan this season after playing two years at UCLA.
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – MARCH 14: Aday Mara #15 of the Michigan Wolverines celebrates against the Wisconsin Badgers in the second half during the semifinals of the 2026 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Tournament at the United Center on March 14, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Michigan lost an essential piece of its well-oiled offense when standout sophomore guard L.J. Cason went down with a torn ACL in February. While coming off the bench, Cason averaged 8.4 and 2.4 assists, hitting more than 40.2% from behind the arc. With his absences, guard Elliot Cadeau has taken up almost all backup point guard duties.
Led by second-year head coach Dusty May, Michigan has all the ingredients to make a deep March Madness run and a real chance to etch its name in the history books as the 2026 national champs.
Howard Howard University, based in Washington, D.C., is one of 107 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs).
The university has made it to the big dance five times, with the last one being in 2024, when they fell to Wagner 71-68 in the First Four. The last time the Bison made it out of the First Four was in 2023, playing the No. 1 seed Kansas in the round of 64. They would lose to the Jayhawks 96-68. Howard’s win over UMBC was the university’s first-ever tournament win.
DAYTON, OHIO – MARCH 17: Stefan Isailovic #1 and Cam Gillus #2 of the Howard Bison react after defeating the UMBC Retrievers in the First Four game of the 2026 NCAA Men’s Basketball Tournament at UD Arena on March 17, 2026 in Dayton, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) Howard finished its regular season with a record of 24-10, the best in the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference (MEAC). The Bison took home the conference championship after defeating North Carolina Central 70-63.
Head coach Kenny Blakeney has been part of legendary tournament runs, just not as a member of the staff. He played for Duke from 1991 to 1995 and won two national championships under legendary coach Mike Krzyzewski.
Blakeney was named head coach of Howard basketball back in 2019. During his tenure, he has led the Bison to three tournament appearances in four years. He also won MEAC Coach of the Year in 2023.
The Bison are led by the backcourt duo of guard Bryce Harris and guard Cedric Taylor III. Harris averages 17.1 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 2.5 assists while shooting 48.4% from the field and 38.7% from behind the arc. Taylor also put up 17.1 points a game, along with 6.7 rebounds and 3.2 assists.
Howard’s lineup is on the smaller side, with only two players standing over 6-foot-8. They are likely to struggle against Michigan’s size and physical play, but the tournament has been dubbed March Madness for a reason.
Where to Watch: Michigan vs. Howard Date: Thu. Mar. 19, 2026 | Time: 7:10 p.m. ET
Location: KeyBank Center, Buffalo, New York
TV: CBS
Streaming: Fubo
Odds: Michigan -30.5
